edition.title: Morning paper, Tuesday 6 October 2026
edition.fact: Five stories on the front page, three short beats below
edition.intro: A sample of the new format. Facts are from sources I read in full; anything resting on one outlet or on a vendor's own numbers is marked. Nothing here is a stock tip.

blocks.title: IRDAI wants to cap what insurers pay distributors

blocks.html: IRDAI's paper "Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution" proposes a company-level expense-of-management cap of 12.5% of gross direct premium for life insurers, and for general insurers a cut from 30% to 20%, phased over five years. The case rests on sampled data: distributor remuneration for a group of corporate agents rose 125% (₹9,580 cr to ₹21,600 cr, FY23 to FY25) while new business premium rose 28%. General insurance broker commissions rose 173% against 37% growth in premium routed. Banks tied to several insurers averaged a 33% payout, up to 72%, against 13% for single-tie-up banks. Group credit life payouts reached up to 45% in FY25, from about 5%.

Why it matters to you: Bank and corporate-agent channels, and broker commissions, are the economics Probus sits on. If the expense cap lands, payout structures get renegotiated, and aggregator take rates are in the frame. It is a consultation paper, so nothing is final.
Source: Moneycontrol, 23 Sep

blocks.title: Banks' deposit growth is flattered by a window that has closed

blocks.html: RBI's concessional swap window for FCNR(B) deposits closed on 31 August, and banks mobilised nearly $133 bn through it. HDFC Bank alone took $11.5 bn, about 8.6% of the inflows. Yes Bank shows how large the effect can be: reported deposit growth of 19.5% year on year is 6.5% once FCNR(B) is removed, and loan growth of 23.8% is 3.3% on the same basis. System credit grew 18.1% and deposits 17.3% as of 15 September (RBI data, via Business Standard). Axis Securities warns of margin pressure from the higher cost of funds.

Why it matters to you: Headline growth at banks in Q2 results season overstates the underlying trend, and the cost of those deposits shows up later in margins. Read adjusted numbers, not reported ones.
Source: Business Standard, 4 Oct / Financial Express, 5 Oct

blocks.title: Foreign investors sold ₹35,861 cr of equities in September; domestic funds are absorbing it

blocks.html: NSDL data puts September FPI equity flow at -₹35,861 cr. By trade date it is closer to -₹45,093 cr, because ₹9,232 cr of 30 September trades were booked in October. FPIs are down ₹2,69,534 cr in 2026 so far. On 5 October, one aggregator reports FIIs net sold ₹4,699 cr while DIIs bought ₹5,182 cr: a seven-session FII sell streak against an eleven-session DII buy streak, and Nifty down 2.53% over five sessions. The 5 October figures come from that single aggregator and I could not cross-check them.
Why it matters to you: This is the flow behind the Nifty's drop, and a watch item before Wednesday's RBI decision. It is a description of flows, not a signal to trade.
Source: Paisa Samjho, citing PTI/Times of India / Flash Finance (single source for the 5 Oct detail)

blocks.title: Google and OpenAI now price new models at $2 per million input tokens

blocks.html: Prices below are per million tokens, from the vendors' own posts and tables. Benchmark claims in those tables are vendor-reported and not independently tested.
Why it matters to you: The price of a prototype that calls a top model just fell by a factor of five against GPT-6 Astra. Cached input at $0.10 on GPT-6.1 Sol makes long-context agents cheap to test.
Source: eWeek on Gemini 4 Argon / Anthropic, Opus 5.5 / OpenAI Developer Community, GPT-6.1 Sol

blocks.title: Indian tech funding is up 7% on fewer, bigger rounds

blocks.html: Tracxn counts $10.3 bn raised in the first nine months of 2026, up 7%, across 1,134 rounds, down 38%. Seed funding fell 37% to $698 M, first-time funded companies fell 30% to 338, and Series A and later rounds fell 23% to 409. There were 18 rounds of $100 M or more. AI infrastructure was the largest theme at $1.2 bn, and enterprise infrastructure rose 436% to $1.6 bn. Six new unicorns had raised about $101 M on average before their unicorn round, and the median path from Series A to unicorn was 4.9 years.
Why it matters to you: If you build, the seed market is the hard one: money is concentrating in later stages and in infrastructure, not in first cheques.
Source: Tracxn 9M 2026 via CXOToday, 24 Sep

blocks.title: Peak XV cut its Honasa stake from 14.80% to 11.50% in one day

blocks.html: On 30 September Peak XV sold 1,07,55,495 shares of Honasa Consumer, taking its holding from 14.80% to 11.50%. Sequoia Capital Global Growth Fund III sold 25,02,289 shares (3.44% to 2.68%), and Redwood Trust sold 75,549. The stock was up 8.30% over the day per ScanX, so the market absorbed the supply. Single source for the share counts.
Why it matters to you: A venture investor exiting after the IPO lock-in is a supply event for consumer-brand listings. Watchlist only.
Source: ScanX, from SEBI Reg 29(2) filing dated 2 Oct

blocks.title: Steel capex is the visible catalyst

blocks.html: Tata Steel is adding 5 mtpa at NINL in Kalinganagar, about ₹40,000 cr. Shyam Metalics signed an MoU to invest ₹50,000 cr in a 9 mtpa plant in Chandrapur, Maharashtra. An MoU is intent, not a commissioned plant.
Why it matters to you: Large announced capex is a lead indicator for banks with infrastructure books and for steel-linked suppliers.
Source: Rediff/PTI on Tata Steel NINL / BusinessLine on Shyam Metalics

blocks.title: RBI decides on Wednesday; the poll leans to a hike

blocks.html: In a Reuters poll, 35 of 61 economists expect a 25 basis point increase to 5.50%. That leaves 26 expecting something else. The decision is on 7 October.
Why it matters to you: It sets the tone for the bank and NBFC spotlight below.
Source: India Today, 5 Oct (Reuters poll)

blocks.title: Sector spotlight, days 1 and 2: banks and NBFCs, and insurance

blocks.html: Banks and NBFCs: HDFC Bank's gross advances rose 16% to ₹32,135 bn, its best sequential loan growth in nine quarters, with deposits up 18.8%; Anup Bagchi becomes MD and CEO on 27 October. Bajaj Finance is raising ₹17,500 cr (₹11,700 cr QIP plus ₹5,800 cr promoter warrants) and AUM grew 26.5% to ₹5,848 bn. AU Small Finance Bank deposits grew 28.6% and advances 27.9%. Insurance: life new business premium rose 33.07% in August to ₹41,198 cr, and 20.4% over April to August to ₹1.97 lakh cr. Retail-weighted premium rose about 13.9%, which is the number closer to underlying retail demand.
Why it matters to you: Both sit under the same two stories above: deposit costs and distribution rules.
Source: Financial Express, 5 Oct / Capital Market, 8 Sep

blocks.title: Simple Energy's $180 M round is most of India's weekly funding

blocks.html: Indian startups raised $233.6 M across 16 deals that week. Simple Energy's $180 M Series C is 77% of it. The other 15 deals add up to about $53.6 M, which is the better read of the typical week.
Why it matters to you: Weekly totals mislead when one deal dominates. The rest of the market raised about $53.6 M.
Source: Inc42, 28 Sep to 2 Oct

blocks.title: A 19-year-old raised $11 M to sell a $3,499 personal-AI computer

blocks.html: Ghost's founder Zain Javaid raised an $11 M seed led by a16z for Core, a $3,499 computer with an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU. The price and funding are from TechCrunch's report; I have not seen sales figures.
Why it matters to you: A hardware answer to a software question: local AI for people who do not want their data in someone's cloud. A useful reference for what investors will back at seed.
Source: TechCrunch, 5 Oct

blocks.title: Etched is fielding funding offers at a $40 B valuation

blocks.html: TechCrunch reports, citing sources, that Etched has received funding offers at a valuation of $40 B. Nothing is signed.
Why it matters to you: AI chip startups are being valued like platforms. Sources say so, and it is not a closed round.
Source: TechCrunch, 5 Oct

blocks.title: Developers say cached-input pricing is the real news on GPT-6.1 Sol

blocks.html: The top comment says cached input pricing is the real news; codecentral puts the release on 29 September and OpenAI's forum thread carries the $0.10 cached input price, half the earlier $0.20. Others in the thread argue Opus 5.5 is better at hard coding. That is opinion, not a test result.
Why it matters to you: It echoes the front-page point: for agent builders, cache cost matters more than headline price.
Source: Hacker News thread, 362 points / Codecentral on the release

blocks.title: Product Hunt's week: agent infrastructure and model routing

blocks.html: The leaderboard for the week of 5 October has Spira Maxima, FastRouter.ai, which routes across 200+ LLMs, and Opengeni, agent infrastructure, near the top.
Why it matters to you: Routing across models is becoming a product category, which fits falling prices.
Source: Product Hunt weekly leaderboard

blocks.title: Anthropic will run Claude inference in India

blocks.html: Per the Times of India, Anthropic is launching in-country Claude inference in India via AWS.
Why it matters to you: In-country inference matters for regulated Indian customers, including insurance.
Source: Times of India, 5 Oct

Reported, not confirmedSeveral outlets report, citing a WSJ story, that OpenAI cancelled an October GPT-6.1 Astra release over safety concerns. I found no primary confirmation, only secondary sites, so I am not treating it as fact.
